correctness.rationale: A cooperator focal and defector focal differ by swapping the status of a distinguished possible co-player. Excluding that individual from the sample, probability (N-ell)/(N-1), yields an additional marginal geometric benefit (b/ell) δ^Q for hypergeometric Q; inclusion yields identical public benefit. This proves exact finite-N hypergeometric Δ(j), including ell=N zero marginal benefit. For H_{M,K,s}(δ), toggling two marked players gives Δ²H=(δ-1)²[s(s-1)/(M(M-1))] H_{M-2,K,s-2}(δ). All factors nonnegative, strictly so for nontrivial size ell>=3 with δ≠1. A discretely convex sequence cannot have separated strictly negative entries, so its nonzero sign changes are at most two, of form +,-,+. With N=4, exact coefficients 5/18,53/240,11/40 and b/c=4 give Δ/c=(1/9,-7/60,1/10), proving minimal sharpness. Independent exact-rational enumeration of all focal co-player subsets at N=4 matched these three values. The finite proof assumes only N>=4 and admissible sample sizes; larger N does not rely on finite verification.
residual_risks: The Fermi direction-of-selection statement requires Fermi imitation applied to expected payoffs, not random realized payoffs before nonlinearity.

originality.rationale: Prior Bernstein gain-sign theory (Peña, Lehmann & Nöldeke 2013/2014) covers general infinite well-mixed multiplayer matrix games and explains why convexity controls sign variation; Peña (2012) handles group-size diversity with infinite-population/binomial limits. The 2026 Llabrés et al. model treats geometric nonlinear benefits and some size mixtures, but not the exact all-size finite-without-replacement hypergeometric curvature identity and smallest four-person reversal in inspected material. The novelty is the finite sampling identity and sharp small-N construction, not the general variation-diminishing principle. Qualified priority risk remains for finite-population extensions of these papers.
residual_risks: Older gain-sign theorems may have a finite hypergeometric specialization in a companion paper not captured by current searches; novelty claims exclude generic Bernstein variation-diminishing.
ArXiv 2026 related preprint has multiple revisions; only inspected relevant model/appendix sections, not certified complete-document noncoverage.

value.rationale: An all-N convexity theorem with group-size-dependent nonlinear geometric benefits is a meaningful structural restriction on otherwise complicated finite-population payoff profiles. Its sharp four-person witness identifies the minimal coexistence of opposing selection directions, and the exact sampling identity is useful in finite-population evolutionary dynamics. The result separates the finite without-replacement regime from known infinite-population Bernstein theory and makes no unsupported fixation or spatial claims.
residual_risks: No general fixation or ESS theorem for the finite stochastic imitation process is asserted.

limitations: Expected-payoff finite, well-mixed without-replacement sampling; nonlinear random-payoff imitation and heterogeneous mixing are excluded.
General gain-sign theory is antecedent, finite hypergeometric theorem is assessed novelty.
